clue.text: Safe low-flying gull, for example

indicators.note: flying means the letters of safe and low are sent off in a new order

explanation.surface: A gull swooping close to the ground is described as safe, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low-flying' looks like a description of the gull, but the hyphenated word splits: the first half is fodder and only 'flying' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is one example of a bird that lives by the sea.

clue.text: Does one put in the ear drop off?

definitions.text: Does one put in the ear drop off?

parts.words: Does one put in the ear drop off?
parts.note: reads as a question about an earring falling out; really it asks for a small stud worn to keep a pierced ear open, which shares its name with a person who nods off

explanation.definitionFit: A plain stud worn in a newly pierced ear has the same name as someone who dozes.

clue.text: Defence of a caricature

definitions.meaning: a formal written justification, as in Plato's account of Socrates' trial
a poor example, as in 'a sorry excuse for a meal'

explanation.definitionFit: A formal vindication bears this name, and a feeble travesty of something is called a poor one 'for' it.

clue.text: Due, like Gray's herd with no leader

indicators.note: having no leader means the first letter of the herd's description is dropped

parts.note: Thomas Gray's Elegy opens with 'The lowing herd wind slowly o'er the lea'

explanation.surface: Something owed is compared with a leaderless herd from a famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard' has 'the lowing herd'; 'with no leader' removes its first letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Money still owed is payable, so it is outstanding.

clue.text: Come to rest on Evangelist's mileposts

parts.note: an aircraft comes to rest when it touches down
Mark is one of the four Gospel writers, so his possessive is the name plus S

explanation.surface: Something settles on the gospel writer's markers along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Mileposts are notable markers by a route, just as prominent features guide travellers.

clue.text: Act the clown with portable sleeping-equipment

parts.note: to act a part is to be it, as in 'be the villain'
a droll is an old word for a jester or buffoon

explanation.surface: A clowning performer comes along with a camping mat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act the clown' reads as one phrase meaning fool around; 'droll' is an archaic noun for a jester, which solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedding rolled up for carrying is a camper's portable bed.

clue.text: Nobleman's heraldic device operating

definitions.note: read as 'nobleman is', so the definition is the noun

parts.note: a bar is a narrow horizontal band on a coat of arms
a machine that is operating is switched on

explanation.surface: A lord's coat of arms is described as working.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the lowest rank in the British peerage holds this title.

clue.text: Half-dead miracle-worker, he makes a set speech

indicators.note: half of the word dead means its first two letters are taken
the letters of miracle are worked into a new arrangement, so worker signals the shuffle

explanation.surface: A half-dead saint who performs miracles gives a formal oration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-dead' gives DE, and 'worker' rearranges MIRACLE into CLAIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator who speaks in a formal, rhetorical manner recites prepared speeches.

clue.text: Counterpart of irregular verbs in Old English

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the abbreviation for the old language
irregular means the letters of verbs are put out of order

explanation.surface: A grammar note about irregular verbs in Old English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' turns VERBS into BVERS, which goes 'in' OE.
explanation.definitionFit: The other side of a coin or a matching opposite is its complement.

clue.text: Elgar variation on the way to being the most grandiose?

indicators.note: a nod to the composer's Enigma Variations, signalling his name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: An Elgar variation is on its way to being his grandest work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' nods to Elgar's Enigma Variations while rearranging his name into a word for big.
explanation.definitionFit: Biggest of all suggests something on the grandest scale.

clue.text: Excitement of Beethoven's third movement

indicators.note: the third letter of the composer's name is picked out

parts.note: motion is movement in general

explanation.surface: The excitement of the third movement of a Beethoven symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third' picks the third letter of Beethoven, E, not a third movement of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong feeling or agitation of mind is a stirring of the heart.

clue.text: Make good bounce back

definitions.meaning: to regain or recoup something lost
to get well again after illness or setback

explanation.definitionFit: Regaining losses and returning to health are both senses of getting back.

clue.text: His is the local course

parts.note: a pub (the local) serves a cheese-and-pickle lunch named after a farm worker, whose own course is the furrow he cuts

explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's regular pub; a classic pub lunch of bread, cheese and pickle bears this worker's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm labourer who tills fields gives his name to a traditional pub meal.

clue.text: Engineers, in time, concur

indicators.note: the engineers are placed inside the word for a long period

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
RE stands for the Royal Engineers of the British Army

explanation.surface: Engineers come to an agreement in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: To see eye to eye is to be of one mind.

clue.text: Sound correspondence?

parts.note: looks like reliable letters; really means matching sounds at the ends of lines of verse

explanation.definitionFit: Words that end with the same sound correspond in their sound, as in poetry.

clue.text: Calling for the last case in the grammar school

indicators.note: the last letter of the word the is taken

parts.note: the vocative is the grammatical case used for addressing someone, taught in Latin lessons at grammar school

explanation.surface: A request for the final case in a school Latin grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last' gives E, the final letter of 'the'; a 'grammar school' is a selective British secondary school traditionally teaching Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that calls forth memories or feelings is said to summon them up.

clue.text: University doctor in new centre is lying

indicators.note: the university and doctor go inside the rearranged centre
new means the letters of centre are made into a fresh order

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A university doctor at a new centre is lying down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CENTRE into RECENT, and UMB goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reclining flat or lying down describes a recumbent posture.

clue.text: Plain tea, perhaps, for contestant?

parts.note: candid means plain-spoken, frank

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of tea could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Ordinary tea might be offered to a competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing for election or competing is a nominee in the race.

clue.text: State of icons in southwest, shattered

indicators.note: shattered means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: SW is the abbreviation for south-west

explanation.surface: Religious icons in the south-west have been smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges ICONS, IN and SW together.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Midwest by the Great Lakes.

clue.text: Woman wantonly alerts loafer

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly, so the letters of alerts are scattered

explanation.surface: A woman carelessly warns an idler.
explanation.definitionFit: A loafer is an idle, good-for-nothing person who wastes time.

clue.text: Foster to drink wine?

parts.note: to sup is to sip or drink
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Encouraging someone to drink wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster is to encourage or back something.

clue.text: Bloomers for ramblers, possibly?

parts.note: seems to be about walkers' knickers; really flowers, since a rambler is a climbing variety of a garden bloom

explanation.definitionFit: Rambler is a climbing type of this flowering shrub, which blooms in gardens.

clue.text: Betting on strange Scottish name for a pouch

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds when a race begins
orra is a Scots word meaning odd or strange

explanation.surface: Betting on an odd Scottish name for a purse.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is 'starting price' in horse-race betting; ORRA is Scots dialect for 'odd'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland dress pouch worn at the front of a kilt.

clue.text: Quiet, please, for the rest of Hamlet

definitions.meaning: Hamlet's dying words are 'The rest is ...', so the rest is this

explanation.definitionFit: Absence of noise, and Hamlet's last line equates 'the rest' with it.

clue.text: Brown in sanctimonious in the main

indicators.note: the second in places the pious abbreviation within the ocean word

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
PI is a shortened form of pious, meaning sanctimonious

explanation.surface: Something brown is found among sanctimonious types at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic term for the open sea; the first 'in' is only a link, and the second does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown colour, as in old photographs.

clue.text: Cylinder jammed?

parts.note: suggests a stuck engine part; really a rolled sponge cake filled with jam

explanation.definitionFit: A rolled sponge cake spread with jam forms a cylinder.

clue.text: Dimensions announced of pines

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, and only its sound counts

parts.note: size means dimensions or measurements

explanation.surface: Measurements of pine trees are declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pines' looks like trees but is the verb, to long for.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to long or yearn, letting out breaths of sorrow.

clue.text: Prepares mine for sailors

definitions.meaning: to salt a mine is to plant ore fraudulently to make it look rich

explanation.definitionFit: Planting ore to deceive buyers, and seasoned seamen, share this word.

clue.text: Nothing right in bookies enclosure, cheating like this

indicators.note: the nothing and right go inside the bookies' enclosure

parts.note: the ring is the area of a racecourse where bookmakers operate
O looks like zero, nothing
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Nothing is right in the bookies' area, where cheating goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to swindle or cheat, a sense taken from the bird.

clue.text: No lire exchanged after the first of April? Banking flap!

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters come behind the April letter
the first letter of April is taken
exchanged means the letters of no lire are swapped around

explanation.surface: No lire exchanged after the start of April: a banking scare!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' is not finance but an aircraft tilting; 'exchanged' rearranges NO LIRE into ILERON.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged wing surface that makes an aircraft roll or bank.

clue.text: Literary culture required in this post?

definitions.meaning: a man of ... is a learned writer; ... means literature
mail is made of written messages

explanation.definitionFit: Learning and literature, and also the written messages that make up mail.

clue.text: Spirit of people driving at Le Mans?

definitions.meaning: the core or soul of something
French motorists fill up with petrol, which French calls by this word

explanation.definitionFit: The vital core of a thing, and the French word for petrol.
